decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit extends the firm's core airfield lighting business with long installed-base lifecycles, so it likely meets aspirations and needs no problemistic search.
The air situation display fits the tower and surveillance portfolio and complements the MLAT system; with modest uncertainty, the firm's slack lets it carry the product rather than drop it.
Training programs are low-cost, recurring service revenue tied to the installed base and support the firm's lifecycle-service strategy, so there is little reason to drop them.
The AGL training course was only mentioned rather than featured and may be merged into broader training offers, but it is cheap to maintain and complements the core lighting business.
The collaboration software is central to the firm's stated direction of collaborative decision-making and integrated operations, so even uncertain results would be carried rather than abandoned.

As the flagship MLAT launch aligned with the strategy of integrated surveillance and automation, it has strong commitment and long sales cycles that justify keeping it despite the post-COVID downturn in airports.
